summary: Defines a method for APPN High Performance Routing nodes to communicate across IP networks, and the APPN enhancements it needs. It also describes an option set for the APPN connection network model over IP.

eli5.summary: An old IBM network language learns to ride over the regular internet roads.

questions: how does ibm appn work over ip
subtitle: APPN and High Performance Routing over Internet Protocol networks.

tldr.problem: APPN (Advanced Peer-to-Peer Networking) is IBM's enterprise network architecture, but it was designed for dedicated network links and the IBM SNA protocol, not for general IP networks.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2353 defines how APPN nodes can communicate over IP and UDP, treating IP as a data-link layer, and defines protocols for link activation, addressing, transmission, and connection networks in the IP environment.
tldr.outcome: APPN and High Performance Routing (HPR) nodes can now operate over standard IP networks, allowing integration of legacy IBM systems with modern IP infrastructure.

today: RFC 2353 is Informational and has not been obsoleted. It documents APPN/HPR over IP networking as standardized by the APPN Implementers' Workshop. While APPN remains in use for legacy IBM systems, modern IP networking and virtual private networks have reduced the need for dedicated APPN protocols in new deployments.

sections.title: Introduction and Architecture
sections.content:
RFC 2353 defines how APPN (Advanced Peer-to-Peer Networking) nodes and the High Performance Routing (HPR) protocol can use IP networks for communication. APPN is IBM's enterprise networking architecture specified in IBM Systems Network Architecture (SNA) standards. This RFC documents how APPN implementers can support IP and UDP as a new data-link control (DLC) layer, allowing HPR nodes to transport SNA session traffic over IP networks.

The document is based on decisions made by the APPN Implementers' Workshop (AIW), an industry consortium of networking vendors, and is classified as a Closed Pages (CP) architecture document, meaning it is detailed enough to enable interoperable implementations.
sections.eli5: This explains how to plug APPN into the internet. It describes all the wiring, addresses, and communication rules so different companies' APPN products can work together over IP.

sections.title: IP as Data Link Control and Node Structure
sections.content:
The native IP DLC treats IP and UDP (User Datagram Protocol) as the link layer for HPR. UDP provides connectionless delivery and is used because HPR already provides error recovery and in-order delivery through the RTP (Rapid Transport Protocol), making TCP's additional services unnecessary. IANA has registered UDP ports 12000 through 12004 for HPR/IP use, allowing port-based prioritization in the IP network.

An HPR/IP node includes a DLC manager, Logical Data Link Control (LDLC) instances for each link, and a link demultiplexer for each IP port. Multiple links can exist between a pair of IP addresses, identified by the source and destination IP addresses and service access point (SAP) addresses. UDP checksum use is recommended to guarantee data integrity.
sections.eli5: The system treats UDP like a telephone line for APPN. Each APPN message gets a UDP header with port numbers that the network uses for prioritization, just like a post office sorts mail by destination.

sections.title: Link Activation and Liveness
sections.content:
Link activation requires node operators to define an IP DLC and ports via configuration services. When an HPR/IP port is defined, parameters include the local IPv4 address, maximum transmission unit (MTU) sizes (default 1461 bytes, accounting for IP and UDP header overhead), retry timers for LDLC, and liveness timer periods (default 10 seconds).

Because UDP is connectionless, LDLC liveness testing is required to detect link failures; the LDLC TEST command and response provide this detection. Liveness can be sent periodically on active links, or optionally suppressed when the link is idle. When a link failure is detected, mechanisms exist to reactivate the link and prevent stale sessions from failing.
sections.eli5: To set up a link, the system defines an IP address, how big messages can be, and how often to check if the connection is still alive. It uses regular ping-like messages to know when something breaks.

sections.title: Transmission Groups and Class of Service
sections.content:
Regular transmission groups (TGs) may be established over HPR/IP links. Configuration services identify a TG by destination control point (CP) name and TG number. For auto-activatable links, both must be pre-configured. When multiple links exist between IP ports, they are distinguished by the SAP address pair.

APPN class of service (COS) function is extended to IP networks by mapping APPN transmission priorities to IP precedence values (the 3-bit field in the IP Type of Service byte). This allows APPN's existing quality-of-service mechanisms to operate in the IP environment. Larger MTU sizes improve performance, while smaller sizes avoid fragmentation when the IP network has smaller path MTU limits.
sections.eli5: Messages are grouped into lanes (TGs), and important messages get higher priority numbers in the IP header so the network forwards them sooner. This keeps quality of service working the same way whether APPN runs on old cables or the internet.

sections.title: Connection Networks and Deployment Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC also describes an optional APPN connection network model that allows HPR nodes to use IP networks without pre-defining all link connections. Nodes can dynamically establish connections based on destination addresses. Network management for HPR/IP uses the same APPN management tools. The document includes guidelines for IPv4-to-IPv6 migration (currently IPv6 is marked as not supported, with default header size allowance of 1441 bytes for future IPv6 support).

Symbolic packet formats are defined in an appendix for LLC commands and responses, and for NLP (Network Layer Packet) frames sent in UI (Unnumbered Information) frames over the IP DLC.
sections.eli5: For flexibility, APPN can also discover and dynamically connect to other nodes without advance planning, much like how the internet routes packets. The system also prepares for future IPv6 support.
